cs.t: Are you able to actually work with the VR glasses? I bought a pair of viture pro glasses thinking I could use them with my (linux) laptop / (android) phone when travelling as a large external monitor. But they were usable for coding, too difficult to read the text, too shakey. Would just give you a headache. It's a cool idea but I decided the technology wasn't there yet and ended up returning them.
cs.th: Your Phone Is an Entire Computer

cs.t: I also have the Viture Pros. They are awesome for airplane/hotel use. Not great as second monitors, as you say optically they aren't perfect and text makes that show a bit more... but if you hook up a steamdeck or want to watch Netflix on the go it's great! Don't get me wrong, they work as a monitor in a pinch on a plane when you need privacy it's just not going to ever replace a real monitor for you.
cs.th: Apple Vision Pro upgraded with M5 chip

cs.t: This is very cool! Love to see the Commodore 64 style of keyboard computer come back. I got the Viture Pro recently and this would be fun to add to that. Ultimately I think this is a very nice form factor both for portable use with XR glasses, and for use with a USB-C dock at home. The XR glasses on the market are still a bit rough, but the nice thing about this kind of setup is that you can replace the computer and the glasses independently, so as the glasses improve (especially looking forward to glasses with high-quality waveguides) you can upgrade.
cs.th: Bento: A Steam Deck in a Keyboard

cs.t: Same with the Viture Pro. The OLED is crisp and colourful but the resolution is too low to be useful for productivity unless they really nail the head tracking, and can support lots of virtual monitors (and they haven't done that).
cs.th: I ditched my laptop for a pocketable mini PC and a pair of AR glasses
